candidates.summary: chromeShot's comment claims --virtual-time-budget=4000 bounds the wait, but nothing bounds the browser's wall clock, so a wedged Chrome blocks the preview forever
candidates.failure_scenario: The flag bounds the page's virtual clock, not the process. chromeShot builds exec.Command with no context and no deadline and blocks in CombinedOutput. The flag list carries --no-sandbox but not --disable-dev-shm-usage, and a GitHub runner's /dev/shm is 64 MB, which is the classic headless-Chrome wedge: the browser starts, never exits, and ScreenshotPairs never returns. Neither .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml nor pr-preview-publish.yml sets timeout-minutes, so the job holds a runner to GitHub's 6 h default and the PR gets no preview and no comment for that push.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/b4-claims-shots_test.go misc/gnopreview/ && cd misc/gnopreview && go test -count=1 -run TestChromeShotHasNoWallClockBound -v ./... — a fake browser that never exits; expect a return, observe the call still blocked at 6 s. Read half: grep -n 'timeout-minutes' .github/workflows/pr-preview*.yml returns nothing; grep -c disable-dev-shm-usage misc/gnopreview/shots.go returns 0.
candidates.evidence:
--- FAIL: TestChromeShotHasNoWallClockBound (6.00s)
    b4_claims_shots_test.go:58: chromeShot still blocked after 6s: exec.Command carries no context and no deadline, and the preview workflows set no timeout-minutes
FAIL	github.com/gnolang/gno/misc/gnopreview	6.004s

grep -n 'timeout-minutes' .github/workflows/pr-preview*.yml -> (no output)
grep -c disable-dev-shm-usage misc/gnopreview/shots.go -> 0
go test -count=1 ./... without the file -> ok github.com/gnolang/gno/misc/gnopreview 0.006s

candidates.summary: shotPlan's godoc calls it the sample photographed when gnoweb changed, but a PR touching gnoweb and a realm never photographs it, leaving comment.go:53's shotGrid call unreachable
candidates.failure_scenario: main.go:147-151 is an if/else-if: len(plan.ChangedRealms) > 0 takes the pairs arm, and Plan.Shots is assigned only in the else-if arm. A PR that edits gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ and any examples realm in the same push (a CSS change plus its docs realm) lands in the mixed branch: Comment writes "This PR changes **gnoweb** and realm sources" and then shotGrid(p.Shots, base) with p.Shots always nil, so the reviewer gets a before/after of the realm and no picture of the chrome change the PR is actually about. comment.go:53 is the only other caller of shotGrid and can never fire.
candidates.verify_by: grep -rn '\.Shots' misc/gnopreview/ — assignment at main.go:151 only, inside the else-if; then cp tests/b4-claims-shots_test.go misc/gnopreview/ && cd misc/gnopreview && go test -count=1 -run TestMixedModeCommentHasNoGnowebSample -v ./... — the mixed branch emits no _shots/ image, and the same branch with Shots set does.
candidates.evidence:
--- PASS: TestMixedModeCommentHasNoGnowebSample (0.00s)

grep -rn '\.Shots' misc/gnopreview/:
  main.go:151:		plan.Shots = Screenshot(cfg.out, c, cfg.chrome)
  main.go:160:		len(c.pages), len(plan.Shots), len(plan.Pairs), cfg.out)
  comment.go:42:		b.WriteString(shotGrid(p.Shots, base))
  comment.go:53:			b.WriteString(shotGrid(p.Shots, base))
main.go:147-151 is `if len(plan.ChangedRealms) > 0 { ...Pairs... } else if plan.Gnoweb { plan.Shots = Screenshot(...) }`, so comment.go:53 (the p.Gnoweb arm of the default branch) is reached only with p.Shots nil. README.md:70 states the intent as "The two are alternatives, never both", which leaves the comment.go:53 call dead either way.

candidates.summary: serve returns the listener as its io.Closer, so the http.Server it built is never Closed and its connections are never drained
candidates.failure_scenario: serve builds an *http.Server and hands back ln. Both callers do `defer srv.Close()` on that listener, which is enough to make Serve return — the //nolint comment's claim holds — but Server.Close is never called, so Chrome's keep-alive connection and any handler in flight are left to the process exit rather than shut down. Harmless in a one-shot binary; it reads as a bug to the next person who reuses serve.
candidates.verify_by: read misc/gnopreview/shots.go:162-173 and the two `defer srv.Close()` sites at lines 70 and 136: the value deferred is the listener, and the *http.Server is unreachable after serve returns.
candidates.evidence: serve returns `ln` (net.Listener) as io.Closer; `srv := &http.Server{...}` is local and never closed.

candidates.summary: findChrome's godoc promises a browser binary, but the os.Stat fallback accepts any non-directory path, executable or not
candidates.failure_scenario: CHROME=/etc/hosts (or a half-downloaded chrome) fails LookPath, then passes `os.Stat(c) == nil && !fi.IsDir()` and is returned as the browser. Every chromeShot then fails with a permission or exec-format error and the preview ships with no images, reported as a per-page screenshot failure rather than a bad browser path.
candidates.verify_by: read misc/gnopreview/shots.go:210-221 — the second arm checks only IsDir; compare with the first arm's exec.LookPath, which checks the executable bit. Adding `fi.Mode()&0o111 != 0` is the whole fix.
candidates.evidence: `if fi, err := os.Stat(c); err == nil && !fi.IsDir() { return c }` — no mode check.
